column3: The Hebrew retains the seed of the kingdom and separately narrates her rising.
The Hebrew has plural hiding agents, without an explicit purpose clause; BSB makes her hiding the child its purpose.
The Hebrew leaves him and her unnamed; BSB supplies Joash and identifies her as his nurse.
The Hebrew repeats the house of the LORD and actively says he brought them; BSB condenses the place reference and uses having them brought.
The Hebrew calls the building the king’s house; BSB uses royal palace.
The Hebrew calls the building the house without explicitly temple here.
The Hebrew explicitly calls them two parts of you and all those going off duty.
The Hebrew says entering the ranks and separately going out and coming in; BSB has approaching the ranks and wherever he goes.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names a spear in the singular; BSB has spears.
The Hebrew names the right and left shoulders of the house; BSB has south and north sides.
The Hebrew leaves the first agent unnamed and has plural agents making him king; BSB names Jehoiada as that agent. It also supplies the people at the clapping.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name outward movement in her coming.
The Hebrew names trumpets beside the king; BSB specifies trumpeters.
The Hebrew separately says he commanded and said to them; BSB condenses these.
The Hebrew says they laid hands on her and separately that she came by the horses’ entrance; BSB joins these with as and explicitly names Athaliah.
The Hebrew repeats between but no separate second covenant-making verb; BSB supplies another making clause.
The Hebrew calls the guards’ appointer the priest, without Jehoiada’s name, and calls the building Baal’s house.
The Hebrew leaves the seated king unnamed and says throne of kings; BSB supplies Joash and royal throne.
The Hebrew joins the killing with and and uses active plural agents; BSB has because and passive killing.
Close to the Hebrew.
